title: Kronecker Product Attention: Memory-Efficient KV Compression via Structured Factorization
summary: KPA replaces standard MHA/GQA/MLA attention parameterization by representing key and value activations as sums of Kronecker products of compact token-dependent factors, with a structured rotary embedding applied only to those factors instead of a decoupled RoPE branch. The cost is that it is an architectural change requiring training from scratch (or at least substantial retraining), plus a new head-split hyperparameter and custom factorization kernels that lack mature framework support. It can fail for this reader because the reported gains are demonstrated only under controlled identical-training conditions at research scale, and the method cannot be applied to existing pretrained checkpoints or API-served models.
rationale: KPA is a pretraining-time architectural choice, so a team constrained to a single 24 GB GPU and third-party APIs cannot deploy it on existing models and can only track it until pretrained KPA checkpoints or fine-tuning conversion methods become available.
technique: Kronecker Product Attention for KV cache compression
